claims.text: The as-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi alloy is an ordered, single-phase hexagonal material.
The as-deposited alloy contains intrinsic residual stresses.
The as-deposited alloy has a high density of microstructural defects.
Controlled sub-critical post-deposition annealing can relieve residual stresses while preserving the alloy's phase and composition.
Controlled post-deposition annealing can reduce defect concentrations without significant grain coarsening.
Grain boundaries and dislocations act as nucleation sites for the first-order magnetostructural transition.
Reducing residual stress and nucleation-site density broadens the magnetostructural transition and makes it less abrupt.
Broadening and smoothing the transition reduces thermal hysteresis and hysteretic energy loss during cycling.
Stress-relief annealing preserves a peak magnetic entropy change comparable to that of the as-deposited alloy.
Annealed samples will have a broader transition than the as-deposited baseline.
Annealed samples will have less thermal hysteresis than the as-deposited baseline.
Annealed samples will retain a large but less abrupt peak magnetic entropy change.
The as-deposited alloy displays a sharp, hysteretic, first-order magnetostructural transition with a large entropy change.
The as-deposited alloy has limited heat-exchange performance because of its bulk nature and internal stresses.
The predicted behavior is limited to annealing conditions that avoid phase decomposition and significant grain coarsening.
The predicted behavior applies across the explored compositional range under low-field magnetic-refrigeration conditions.
